questions.q: The most suitable method to separate iodine from common salt is:
questions.explain: Iodine passes directly from solid to vapour on heating while NaCl does not, so the iodine condenses as pure crystals on a cold surface and the salt stays behind.

questions.q: On a TLC plate a spot moves 2.4 cm from the base line while the solvent front moves 8.0 cm. The Rf value of the substance is:
questions.explain: Rf = distance moved by substance ÷ distance moved by solvent = 2.4 ÷ 8.0 = 0.30. Rf has no unit and is always less than 1, which rules out 3.33.

questions.q: The stationary phase in paper chromatography is:
options: Cellulose fibres acting as an adsorbent
Silica gel coated on the paper
Water held in the fibres of the paper
questions.explain: Water trapped in the paper fibres is the stationary phase, so paper chromatography is partition chromatography, not adsorption chromatography like TLC or column chromatography.

questions.q: In column chromatography of a mixture of three compounds A, B and C on alumina, A is the most strongly adsorbed and C the least. Which statement is correct?
options: A is eluted first and has the highest Rf on a TLC plate of the same adsorbent
C is eluted last because it interacts least with the stationary phase
A is eluted last and would show the smallest Rf on a TLC plate of the same adsorbent
All three elute together because Rf does not depend on adsorption
questions.explain: The most strongly adsorbed compound moves most slowly, so it is eluted last and, on TLC, travels the shortest distance (smallest Rf). A higher Rf means weaker adsorption.
